# BLOCK - #334 round 1

Role: reviewer/334. Head: 8f705b4ee8308018e235f2c64ed77912e3bc8133.

## B334-R1-01: renewal during the drain's settle still types an obsolete restart

`crates/daemon/src/pointer/worker.rs:419-440` reads the receiver edge and runs
`restart_overtaken` before `copilot_control_held` waits 250 ms between its pane
reads (`worker.rs:552-565`). The same earlier edge is then reused by the
duplicate brake. There is no receiver-edge refresh before command submission.

Reproduction on an isolated exact-head source copy, with no product-source
changes: enqueue the parent's restart while the latest edge is a lapse and
the row remains Working; let the pane show an empty idle composer; publish
renewed after the first launch-free capture, during the settle. The control
then types `/restart`: expected 0 submissions, observed 1. This models a
human restart renewing the extension while an older parent control is being
claimed, or a restarted drain without the earlier in-memory duplicate entry.
It violates the promised "queued before renewal -> fail untyped" rule and
can restart an already recovered Copilot again.

Required fix: refresh the receiver edge after the slow checks at the final
submission boundary and apply the overtaken-control brake to that fresh edge.
Keep the narrow regression that renews specifically between pane reads, plus
the positive case admitting a new restart after renewal. No new policy is
needed: these are one-directional brakes, not policies.

## Other requested conclusions

- The supported captured screens classify correctly: both composer layouts,
  narrow footer, status text other than Working, multi-line drafts, unknown
  rows and missing/mismatched composer boundaries. A status lacking the busy
  markers and all footer markers holds as unreadable. No busy/draft-to-Idle
  misclassification was reproduced on the supported fixtures; this does not
  certify arbitrary future Copilot layouts.
- The drain selects lapsed from the latest spine receiver edge, but only at
  the initial read: B334-R1-01 is the missing refresh. F261 separately rechecks
  the in-memory renewal before recording/queuing.
- A restart admitted after a renewal still types: the independent positive
  regression passes. Ordinary heartbeat renewals do not emit a new renewed
  edge unless ending a told lapse (`delivery/mod.rs:509-533`).
- The duplicate grace lasts 60 seconds in daemon memory, not across a daemon
  restart. `worker.rs:569-596` explicitly describes that limit; the API calls
  it "in the daemon's memory" and says that past 60 seconds it types as before.
- The merge is clean. `git diff --check` passes; the difficulty ledger retains
  D-F276-1, D-F276-2 and D-F278-1, adding only D-F279-1 against main 3707709e.
- Cost from source: no new timer, loop or daemon launch site. Existing drain
  claims are at most one per seat per 5-second pass, with 1-second to 5-minute
  backoff. Each Copilot control adds a latest-edge read; lapsed claims take
  one or two launch-free captures in place of registry-state reads. A restart
  against a renewed edge also reads its admission. `capture_without_launch`
  uses `query_live`, which never starts/replaces a client and returns None
  when unavailable, causing HOLD. The independent performance role owns live
  rate receipts and the after-deploy measurement.

## Harness lesson

magicWand: extend the existing recovery suite with a fake-tmux capture barrier
that publishes a receiver renewal between the two pane reads. Testing renewal
only before a drain claim misses the asynchronous gap this brake introduces.
The isolated review regression demonstrates the exact failing sensor to retain.

difficulties: the dependency-free review tree cannot satisfy the full TS
inventory under C25; the first recovery selector used its source-file name
and selected zero tests, corrected to the actual `auth_recovery` module (29).
Shared target contention was handled by the existing lock, never another target.
No product or governance ledger was edited by hand.

## Minimal regression to retain

Add to the existing `auth_recovery_tests.rs` suite; it uses that suite's fleet,
edge, parent-restart and drain helpers, and never accesses a live pane:

```rust
#[tokio::test]
async fn review334_renewal_during_settle_closes_restart_untyped() {
    let fleet = fleet(SystemState::Working, None).await;
    edge(&fleet, crate::delivery::NATIVE_RECEIVER_LAPSED, Some(SEAT)).await;
    parent_restart(&fleet, "parent-before-renewal").await;
    let worker = drain(&fleet);
    let renew = async {
        let started = Instant::now();
        while !fleet.tmux.calls().iter().any(|call| {
            call == &format!("capture_without_launch:{PANE}")
        }) {
            assert!(started.elapsed() < Duration::from_secs(5));
            tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(1)).await;
        }
        edge(&fleet, crate::delivery::NATIVE_RECEIVER_RENEWED, Some(SEAT)).await;
    };
    let (result, ()) = tokio::join!(worker.drain_once(), renew);
    result.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(restarts_typed(&fleet), 0);
    assert!(controls(&fleet).await.is_empty());
}
```
